picks.headline: AI가 20년치 아르고 관측으로 대서양 순환을 복원하다
picks.excerpt: Helmholtz researchers combined machine learning with established physical models to reconstruct Atlantic Ocean circulation from 20 years of Argo profiling-float data, extracting more signal from sparse measurements than physics-only methods. The hybrid approach sharpens understanding of key circulation systems that drive climate.
picks.rationale: Climate/ocean pick: a hybrid ML-plus-physics method that pulls more signal from sparse Argo float data than physics-only models, improving how ocean scientists reconstruct climate-driving circulation. Distinct study and URL from the 07-22 GOFLOW ocean-current card.

picks.headline: AI가 DNA 가닥끼리의 결합을 83.5% 정확도로 예측하다
picks.excerpt: North Carolina State University researchers built an AI model, BINND, that predicts which DNA molecules will bind to each other with 83.5% accuracy after training on 144 million sequence pairs, beating prior methods by at least 10%. Better modeling of these hypercomplex binding relationships could aid biomedical diagnostics and DNA computing.
picks.rationale: Life-science pick: a concrete new model (BINND) that beats prior methods by 10%+ on DNA-DNA binding prediction, a foundational capability for diagnostics and DNA computing. Fresh topic and outlet-distinct from the earlier biomanufacturing card.

picks.headline: 열 요동을 계산 자원으로 삼는 열역학 컴퓨터의 부상
picks.excerpt: Quanta surveys a new class of thermodynamic computers that harness random thermal fluctuations as a computational resource rather than fighting them, aiming to run generative-AI algorithms with orders-of-magnitude less energy. Physicists like Normal Computing's Patrick Coles argue exploiting thermodynamics could reshape the hardware substrate of AI.
picks.rationale: Physics pick from a top-credibility outlet (Quanta): a novel hardware paradigm that exploits thermal noise to run generative AI with far less energy. Genuine physics research intersecting AI, not industry noise, and the run's only physics-substrate story.

picks.headline: AI는 '분위기'를 읽을 수 있는가 — 관건은 맥락이다
picks.excerpt: Psychologist Michael Hogan describes research using AI-driven analytics to code non-verbal behavior such as silence during group work at millisecond precision, finding that identical pauses carry different meanings by context. The takeaway: the hard problem is not teaching AI to notice behavior, but to interpret it in context.
picks.rationale: Psychology/behavior pick: AI-driven millisecond coding of non-verbal cues (silence in group work) reframes the hard problem as context interpretation, not detection. Adds a distinct behavioral-science angle and a third outlet to the spread.
